set.prevailing_wage_basis: Not triggered. The City of Napa Junior Unit Program Guidelines (rev. August 2022) state that the Program finances rehabilitation of privately owned, single-family owner-occupied homes and that construction funded by the Program satisfies the prevailing wage exemption in Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(C) (assistance to a household for rehabilitation of a single-family home). The program is limited to JADUs carved from the existing home and conversion of existing accessory structures, not new detached construction. HCD PLHA guidelines (2019 and 2024-2028) contain no prevailing wage provision. https://www.cityofnapa.org/DocumentCenter/View/5224 ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720 ; https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf
set.typical_award_size: Napa's PLHA formula allocation is programmed 80% to Junior and Accessory Dwelling Unit creation, 15% to homeless services and 5% to administration. The Junior Unit Initiative provides a 0% forgivable loan of up to $75,000 to create a JADU or converted ADU (forgiven 5% per year over 20 years), an additional interest free deferred loan of up to $25,000 for converted ADUs, grants up to $5,000 for ADA improvements, design and engineering grants, and free construction management (2026 flyer). Owner must occupy one unit and rent the other to a low income tenant under a recorded regulatory agreement.
set.per_unit_cap: $75,000 forgivable plus up to $25,000 deferred per converted ADU, plus up to $5,000 ADA grant.
set.affordability_requirement: Rental unit affordable to a household at or below 80% AMI at the City's posted affordable rents for 20 years under a recorded regulatory agreement; owner occupies the other unit. (The delegated city PLHA plans use a 10 year term.)
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set false on the program guidelines' own Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(C) exemption statement. Also corrected loan size from $50,000 to $75,000 forgivable and the City program term from 10 to 20 years per the 2026 flyer and August 2022 guidelines.

reason: Program guidelines state the 1720(c)(5)(C) single-family rehab exemption applies, and the 2026 flyer shows a $75,000 forgivable loan and 20 year term rather than $50,000 and 10 years.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program rule found. The American Canyon PLHA plan (City of Napa as delegated administrator) is silent on prevailing wage and describes loans to create ADUs or JADUs, not only conversions. HCD PLHA guidelines (2019 and 2024-2028) have no prevailing wage provision. The City of Napa Junior Unit guidelines claim the Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(C) single-family rehab exemption, but they cover only properties in the City of Napa and only JADUs and conversions; American Canyon guidelines were not located. Coverage otherwise rests on Labor Code 1720(b) public funds and depends on 1720(c) facts, such as (c)(5)(C) for rehab of a single-family home or (c)(1) for private residential projects on private property. https://www.cityofnapa.org/DocumentCenter/View/10393/2022-PLHA-Formula-Application---American-Canyon-PDF ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Tier 3: left unclear. American Canyon plan and PLHA guidelines silent; Napa's 1720(c)(5)(C) exemption statement applies to Napa's own conversion-only program and may not cover new ADU construction in American Canyon. Confirm with City of Napa Housing Division.

reason: No stated prevailing wage rule for the American Canyon program; outcome depends on Labor Code 1720(c) facts such as whether the ADU is rehab of a single-family home.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program rule found. Housing Element Program H-CC (HCD review draft) is silent on prevailing wage and St. Helena has not adopted written fee relief criteria. Reduced, deferred or waived fees are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4), but coverage depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts, such as (c)(3) de minimis, (c)(5)(E) for qualifying below-market loans, and the other public funds in the deal (trust fund, Measure E). https://www.hcd.ca.gov/housing-elements/docs/saint-helena-6th-draft090722.pdf ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Tier 3: left unclear. Housing Element searched for prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon and public works with no program rule; only basis is Labor Code 1720(b)(4), which depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.

reason: No stated prevailing wage rule for St. Helena fee relief; fee waivers count as public funds under 1720(b)(4) but coverage turns on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.
